mainTopic: Which olive oils are fit for מנחות and the מנורה: unripe-olive oil, unfit oils, and the three harvests with their nine grades of oil
overview: The amud opens by setting the משנה against a ברייתא. The משנה says a מנחה brought with oil from unripe olives is פסול, while the ברייתא says it is כשר because that liquid is only sap. רב יוסף answers that רבי חייא threw this oil away, while רבי שמעון בר רבי dipped his food in it, and each source follows one of them. A side discussion then explains the 'שמן המור' of מגילת אסתר: either a perfumed oil, or oil from olives that have not reached a third of their growth, which removes hair and softens the skin. A ברייתא adds sediment oil and bad-smelling oil to the oils that are פסול for a מנחה. רבה then asks whether consecrating such oil earns lashes like a בעל מום, and the question ends in תיקו. A new משנה describes three olive harvests, each giving three grades of oil, with the first grade for the מנורה and the rest for מנחות. The גמרא uses a ברייתא to show that the wording is מגלגלו, and explains that our משנה agrees with רבי יהודה on one point and disagrees on another. A final משנה ranks the nine oils and uses the פסוק 'זך כתית למאור' to show that refined oil is needed only for the מנורה.

steps.title: The משנה and a ברייתא disagree about unripe-olive oil
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says a מנחה brought with this oil is פסול, but a ברייתא says it is כשר because the liquid is only sap.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And if he brought it, it is not valid.' But a ברייתא teaches: 'If he brought it, it is valid, because it is only sap.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that our משנה and a ברייתא give opposite rulings about a מנחה brought with oil from unripe olives.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה rules פסול. That means it treats this liquid as real oil, just a poor kind of oil that should not be used. The ברייתא rules כשר because the liquid is not oil at all, only sap (שרף), so it does not count as bringing bad oil. So the real question is whether this liquid counts as oil.

keyTerms.meaning: Invalid; the offering does not count
Valid; the offering counts
Sap or resin; a plant juice that is not real oil

steps.confusionAlert: Don't misread the ברייתא. It says כשר because this liquid is not considered oil at all. It is not saying that bad oil is fine to use.

phrases.english: And if he brought it, it is not valid
phrases.notes: This is the end of the משנה. It is talking about a מנחה made with oil from unripe olives (אנפקנון).

phrases.english: But isn't it taught: if he brought it, it is valid,
phrases.notes: Some versions don't have the words in round brackets. Here we read them as the ברייתא that challenges the משנה.

phrases.english: because it is only sap.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the discussion by setting the משנה against a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling of the משנה that a מנחה with unripe-olive oil is פסול.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא rules the opposite, כשר, because it sees the liquid as sap and not as oil.

steps.title: רב יוסף: two sages saw this oil differently
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא follows רבי חייא, who threw this oil away. The משנה follows רבי שמעון בר רבי, who dipped his food in it. The memory aid is 'the rich are stingy.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: It is not a problem. This follows רבי חייא and that follows רבי שמעון בר רבי. רבי חייא would throw it away, and רבי שמעון בר רבי would dip his food in it. Your memory aid: the rich are stingy.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף settles the contradiction. He says the משנה and the ברייתא reflect two sages who treated this oil differently in real life.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חייא threw the oil away, so to him it was not real oil, only sap. That fits the ברייתא's ruling of כשר. רבי שמעון בר רבי used it as oil for dipping, so to him it was real oil, though poor oil. That fits the משנה's ruling of פסול.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; the opening words of an answer
Throws away
Dips food into it
Your memory aid
The rich are stingy; they don't waste anything

steps.whatToRemember: Whether this liquid is 'oil' depends on how people treat it. רבי חייא's view (just sap) leads to כשר, and רבי שמעון בר רבי's view (real oil) leads to פסול.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the גמרא deciding a halachic category ('is this oil?') by looking at how people actually use the substance.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: It is not difficult,
this follows Rabbi Ḥiyya,
phrases.notes: 'This' is the ברייתא that says כשר.

phrases.english: that follows Rabbi Shimon, son of Rabbi,
phrases.notes: 'That' is our משנה that says פסול.

phrases.english: for Rabbi Ḥiyya would throw it away,
and Rabbi Shimon, son of Rabbi, would dip into it,
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets ('in it') is the corrected wording; the word in round brackets is left out.

phrases.english: And your memory aid: the rich are stingy.
phrases.notes: רבי שמעון was the son of the wealthy רבי, and he did not waste even this oil.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigns each source to a different sage (תנאי היא).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It seemed that the משנה and the ברייתא simply contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each source follows a different sage. Their disagreement is whether unripe-olive oil counts as real oil.

steps.title: What is the 'oil of myrrh' in מגילת אסתר?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns to a side topic and asks what the 'שמן המור' in the פסוק is.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Six months with oil of myrrh.' What is 'oil of myrrh'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a related side topic. It quotes the פסוק about how the women prepared for אחשורוש and asks what 'שמן המור' means. This sets up the answers in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a new topic, not part of the earlier question and answer. It is connected because one answer will also be about unripe-olive oil, the same oil discussed above.

keyTerms.meaning: Oil of myrrh; mentioned in אסתר 2:12
What is

phrases.english: 'Six months with oil of myrrh' –
what is 'oil of myrrh'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A side topic, linked to step 2 by the subject of unripe-olive oil.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What substance the פסוק calls 'שמן המור'.

steps.title: Two answers: a perfumed oil, or unripe-olive oil
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בר חייא says it is סטכתא. רבי ירמיה בר אבא says it is oil from olives that have not reached a third of their growth.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא בר חייא said: It is סטכתא. רבי ירמיה בר אבא said: It is olive oil from olives that have not reached one-third of their growth.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים explain what 'שמן המור' is, and each gives a different answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא בר חייא says it is a known perfumed oil called סטכתא. רבי ירמיה בר אבא says it is the oil of very unripe olives. That is the same oil the משנה said should not be used for a מנחה.

keyTerms.meaning: A fragrant oil, probably from myrrh
Olive oil
Olives that have not reached a third of their growth

phrases.aramaic: רַב הוּנָא בַּר חִיָּיא אָמַר: סְטָכְתָּא.
phrases.english: Rav Huna bar Ḥiyya says: It is setakhta.
Rabbi Yirmeya bar Abba says:
Olive oil from olives that have not reached one-third of their growth.

steps.triggerLanguage: רב הונא בר חייא אמר: סטכתא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Either the perfumed oil סטכתא, or oil from olives under a third of their growth.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports the unripe-olive-oil view
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה teaches that אנפקנון is oil from olives under a third of their growth, and that women spread it on their skin to remove hair and soften the skin.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is also taught in a ברייתא: רבי יהודה says: אנפקנון is olive oil from olives that have not reached a third of their growth. Why do women spread it on? Because it removes hair and softens the skin.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that backs up רבי ירמיה בר אבא's explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא shows that this unripe-olive oil was used as a beauty treatment: it removed hair and softened the skin. That fits the women's preparation in מגילת אסתר, so it supports רבי ירמיה בר אבא.

keyTerms.meaning: Oil from unripe olives
Spread or rub on the body
Makes fall off; removes hair
Softens and pampers

steps.whatToRemember: אנפקנון, oil from olives under a third of their growth, is too poor for a מנחה, but it was valued for skin care. That is why רבי ירמיה בר אבא identifies it as the 'שמן המור.'

phrases.english: This is also taught:
Rabbi Yehuda says: anpikanon is
olive oil from olives that have not reached one-third of their growth,
why do they spread it on?
Because it removes the hair
and softens the skin.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the second answer in step 4.
steps.raayaObject: רבי ירמיה בר אבא's view that שמן המור is unripe-olive oil.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא of רבי יהודה describing אנפקנון and its use in skin care.

steps.title: Oil from soaked olives and other unfit oils
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's ruling about olives soaked in water (and pickled or boiled olives), then brings a ברייתא that adds sediment oil and bad-smelling oil to the list of oils that are פסול for a מנחה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: one may not bring oil from olives that were soaked in water. The ברייתא adds: olive oil from pickled, boiled, or soaked olives, oil from the sediment, and oil with a bad smell should not be brought. If someone did bring it, it is פסול.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to another line of the משנה and backs it up with a ברייתא that gives a longer list of unfit oils.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה already listed olives soaked in water, pickled olives, and boiled olives. The ברייתא repeats those and adds two more cases: oil from the sediment and oil with a bad smell. All of these are פסול even after the fact (בדיעבד).

keyTerms.meaning: olives (individual olive berries)
pickled, preserved in liquid
boiled
sediment, the dregs left at the bottom

phrases.english: One may not bring from the olives
that were soaked in water.
The Sages taught:
Olive oil from pickled, boiled, or soaked olives,
and oil from sediment, and oil with a bad smell –
one should not bring it, and if he brought it, it is invalid.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין מְבִיאִין מִן הַגַּרְגְּרִין שֶׁנִּשְׁרוּ בְּמַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the side topic about שמן המור, the גמרא returns to explain another line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Oil from pickled, boiled, or soaked olives, sediment oil, and bad-smelling oil may not be brought for a מנחה. If it was brought, it is פסול.

steps.title: Does consecrating unfit oil earn lashes like a blemished offering?
steps.stepSummary: רבה asks whether someone who consecrates this unfit oil gets lashes, as he would for consecrating a בעל מום.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה asked: if someone consecrated this unfit oil, does he get lashes for it because of the rule against a blemished offering? Do we say that since it is unfit, it is like a blemished animal? Or maybe the rule of בעל מום only applies to an animal?
steps.whatsHappening: רבה asks a real question that goes one step beyond the ruling that this oil is פסול: is there also a punishment for consecrating it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a prohibition, punished by lashes, against consecrating a blemished animal for the מזבח. One side says: unfit oil is just like a blemished animal, so the same prohibition applies. The other side says: the rule of בעל מום was only said about animals, not about oil.

keyTerms.meaning: he consecrated it, set it aside as holy for the מקדש
he gets lashes (מלקות)
a blemished animal, unfit for the מזבח
or perhaps, introducing the other side of a question

phrases.english: Rabbah asked:
If he consecrated it, what is the law:
does he get lashes for it because of the rule of a blemished offering?
Since it is unfit, is it like a blemished animal?

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִלְמָא אֵין בַּעַל מוּם אֶלָּא בִּבְהֵמָה?
phrases.english: Or perhaps the rule of a blemished offering applies only to an animal?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the ברייתא's ruling that these oils are פסול and asks whether there is also a punishment for consecrating them.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the prohibition against consecrating a בעל מום, with its lashes, also apply to unfit oil, or only to animals?

steps.title: The question stays unresolved
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא ends רבה's question with תיקו: no answer is found.
steps.simpleTranslation: The question stands unresolved.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes רבה's question without deciding it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No source settles whether unfit oil counts like a בעל מום. So it is left open, and we do not know if there are lashes for consecrating it.

keyTerms.meaning: let it stand; the question remains unresolved

steps.whatToRemember: Unfit oil is פסול for a מנחה, but whether consecrating it earns lashes like a בעל מום is left as תיקו.

phrases.english: Let it stand unresolved.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends רבה's question with no answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: It stays undecided whether someone who consecrates unfit oil gets lashes as he would for a בעל מום.

steps.title: New משנה: three harvests, three oils each
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה opens by saying there are three olive harvests, and each harvest gives three grades of oil.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: There are three olive harvests, and from each of them come three kinds of oil.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with a general rule. The rest of the משנה will explain it harvest by harvest.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The olives on a tree do not all ripen at the same time, so they are picked in three rounds. From each round, three grades of oil are made, from the finest down to the weakest.

keyTerms.meaning: short for מתניתין, our משנה
olives; here, olive harvests
oils, grades of oil

phrases.english: Mishnah:
There are three olive harvests,
phrases.notes: Literally "three olives." It means three rounds of picking during the year.

phrases.english: and in each of them, three oils.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה starts after the previous discussion ended with תיקו.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There are three olive harvests, and each one gives three grades of oil.

steps.title: How the first oil of the first harvest is made
steps.stepSummary: The משנה describes the first harvest: picking the ripe olives at the top of the tree, crushing them, and putting them in a basket. רבי יהודה says to put them around the basket's sides. This gives the first oil.
steps.simpleTranslation: The first harvest: one picks the olives at the top of the tree, crushes them, and puts them inside the basket. רבי יהודה says: around the sides of the basket. This is the first oil.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה starts to explain its general rule, beginning with the best oil from the first harvest. רבי יהודה disagrees about where in the basket the olives are placed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The olives at the top of the tree ripen first, so they are picked first. After crushing, the oil drips out through the basket on its own, without pressing. The תנא קמא puts the olives inside the basket, while רבי יהודה puts them around its sides.

keyTerms.meaning: he picks it olive by olive
crushes, pounds
basket
around, along the sides

phrases.english: The first olive harvest:
one picks the olives at the top of the olive tree,
and crushes them and places them inside the basket.
Rabbi Yehuda says: around the sides of the basket.
This is the first oil.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins explaining the משנה's general rule, starting with the first oil of the first harvest.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The first oil comes from olives picked at the top of the tree, crushed, and placed in a basket so the oil drips out. רבי יהודה says to place them around the basket's sides.

steps.title: Pressing out the second grade of oil
steps.stepSummary: After the first oil drips out on its own, a beam is pressed on the olives to get more oil. רבי יהודה says stones are used instead. This gives the second grade.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then he presses down on the olives with a wooden beam. רבי יהודה says he uses stones. This is the second oil.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues the first harvest and explains how the second grade of oil is made: by pressing the olives with weight.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first oil only dripped out by itself. Now force is added, so this oil is a lower grade. רבי יהודה disagrees only about the tool: he says stones should be used, not a beam.

keyTerms.meaning: Presses down by putting a weight on top
A heavy wooden beam used for pressing
Stones placed on the olives as a lighter weight

phrases.english: He then presses down with a beam,
Rabbi Yehuda says: with stones
– this is the second oil.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the first-harvest process from step 10, moving from the first oil to the second.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The second grade of oil comes from pressing the olives with a beam (תנא קמא) or with stones (רבי יהודה).

steps.title: Grinding out the third grade of oil
steps.stepSummary: The olives are ground and pressed again. This gives the third and lowest grade of oil.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then he grinds the olives and presses them again. This is the third oil.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes the first harvest by describing the third and last grade of oil.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the olives are fully ground up, not just crushed, and then pressed. This squeezes out whatever oil is left, so it is the lowest of the three grades.

keyTerms.meaning: Ground the olives fine, as in a mill
The third grade of oil

phrases.english: He then ground them, and pressed down
– this is the third oil.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the list of three grades from the first harvest.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The third grade of oil comes from grinding the olives and then pressing them.

steps.title: Which oil is used for the מנורה and which for מנחות
steps.stepSummary: Only the first grade of oil may be used to light the מנורה. All the other grades may be used for מנחות.
steps.simpleTranslation: The first oil is for the מנורה, and the rest are for מנחות.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now gives the practical ruling: what each grade of oil may be used for.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מנורה needs the purest oil, so only the first oil (the one that dripped out by itself) is fit for it. The lower grades are still fit for מנחות.

keyTerms.meaning: The golden lamp in the מקדש, lit with olive oil
Flour offerings, which are mixed with oil
The rest: here, the second and third grades

steps.whatToRemember: First oil goes to the מנורה; second and third oil go to מנחות.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the lower grades are פסול. They are still fit for מנחות; they just are not fit for the מנורה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the main halachic point of the whole description of harvests and grades.

phrases.english: The first oil – is for the Menorah,
phrases.notes: The מנורה needs very pure oil, as in ויקרא 24:2.

phrases.english: and the rest – are for meal offerings.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the ruling about the three grades just described.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only the first grade of oil may be used for the מנורה; the other grades may be used for מנחות.

steps.title: The second harvest and its first oil
steps.stepSummary: For the second harvest, the olives that can be reached from the rooftop are picked, crushed, and put in a basket. רבי יהודה says to put them around the sides of the basket. This gives the first oil.
steps.simpleTranslation: The second harvest: he picks the olives that can be reached from the top of the roof, crushes them, and puts them into the basket. רבי יהודה says: around the sides of the basket. This is the first oil.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves to the second of the three harvests and begins describing its first grade of oil.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The process is the same as in the first harvest. What changes is which olives are picked: now the olives reachable from the rooftop. רבי יהודה again says the olives go around the sides of the basket.

keyTerms.meaning: Picks the olives one by one
The top of the roof, where one stands to reach these olives
Crushes, as in a mortar
Around the sides

phrases.english: The second harvest – he picks it at the top of the roof,
and crushes, and puts it into the basket,
Rabbi Yehuda says: around the sides of the basket
– this is the first oil.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing the first harvest, the משנה starts on the second harvest, using the same pattern as step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the second harvest, the olives reachable from the roof are picked, crushed, and placed in (or around the sides of) the basket to produce the first oil.

steps.title: Second harvest: pressing with a beam gives the second grade
steps.stepSummary: For the second harvest, after the first oil drips out, a beam is pressed on the olives. רבי יהודה says stones are used instead. This oil is the second grade.
steps.simpleTranslation: He presses down with a beam. רבי יהודה says: with stones. This is the second grade.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה goes on with the second harvest. It tells us how the second grade of oil is made from these olives.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same method used for the first harvest in Step 11, now applied to the second harvest's olives. Once the first, self-dripping oil is done, pressure squeezes out more oil. רבי יהודה again holds that only stones are used, not a beam.

keyTerms.meaning: Presses down, puts weight on top
A heavy wooden beam used in an olive press
Stones, used as a lighter weight
Second (grade of oil)

phrases.english: He presses down with a beam,
phrases.notes: This is still the second harvest's olives, after their first oil has already dripped out (Step 14).

phrases.english: and רבי יהודה says: with stones –
this is the second grade.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the second-harvest process started in Step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the second harvest, oil squeezed out by pressing (a beam, or according to רבי יהודה stones) is the second grade.

steps.title: Second harvest: grinding and pressing again gives the third grade
steps.stepSummary: The olives of the second harvest are ground and pressed one more time. This gives the third grade of oil.
steps.simpleTranslation: He went back and ground the olives and pressed them. This is the third grade.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes making oil from the second harvest. The last bit of oil, from grinding and pressing, is the third grade.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Grinding breaks the olives down completely, so the pressing now gets out whatever oil is left. This matches Step 12 for the first harvest. Here רבי יהודה does not disagree.

keyTerms.meaning: Went back and did it again
Ground (crushed fine, like with a millstone)
Third (grade of oil)

phrases.english: He went back and ground, and pressed –
this is the third grade.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next stage of processing the same second-harvest olives.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the second harvest, oil from grinding and pressing again is the third grade.

steps.title: Second harvest: only the first grade goes to the מנורה
steps.stepSummary: Of the second harvest's oils, only the first grade may be used for the מנורה. The rest may be used for מנחות.
steps.simpleTranslation: The first grade is for the מנורה, and the rest are for מנחות.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the rule for using the second harvest's oils. It is the same rule as for the first harvest.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מנורה needs the purest oil, so only the first grade, the oil that dripped out by itself, is allowed. The second and third grades are still fine for מנחות. This repeats the rule from Step 13, now for the second harvest.

keyTerms.meaning: The golden lamp in the בית המקדש, lit with pure olive oil
Meal offerings, which are mixed with oil
The rest, the remaining grades

phrases.english: The first grade – for the מנורה,
and the rest – for מנחות.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the usage rule for the three grades made in Steps 14-16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: From the second harvest, only first-grade oil may light the מנורה; the other grades may be used for מנחות.
steps.whatToRemember: For both the first and the second harvest, the rule is the same: only the first, self-dripping oil goes in the מנורה. The other grades are still good for מנחות.

steps.title: Third harvest: softening, drying, then crushing gives the first grade
steps.stepSummary: For the third harvest, the olives are packed in the olive-press building until they soften. Then they are brought up and dried on the roof, crushed, and put in a basket. רבי יהודה says around the basket's sides. This is the first grade.
steps.simpleTranslation: The third harvest: he packs it in the olive-press building until it softens. Then he brings it up and dries it on the roof. He crushes it and puts it into the basket. רבי יהודה says: around the sides of the basket. This is the first grade.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה begins the third and last harvest. These leftover olives are not ripe, so they need extra steps before the first oil can be made.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These are the olives still left on the tree, which have not fully ripened. So they are first left to soften in the press building, then dried on the roof to remove bad-smelling liquid. After that, the crushing and basket step is the same as before, and the oil that drips out is called the first grade of this harvest.

keyTerms.meaning: Packs it into a vat
The building with the olive press
That it softens (gets soft and weak)
Dries it
Crushes (as in a mortar)
A wicker basket, which lets oil drip through

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the grade numbers and the harvest numbers. 'זה ראשון' here means the first grade of oil from the third harvest, not the first harvest.

phrases.english: The third harvest: he packs it into a vat in the olive-press building,
until it softens,
and he brings it up and dries it on top of the roof,
he crushes it and puts it into the basket.
רבי יהודה says: around the sides of the basket –
this is the first grade.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the second harvest to the third harvest, following the same pattern with extra preparation steps.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the third harvest, the olives are softened and dried before crushing; the oil that drips from the basket is that harvest's first grade.

steps.title: Third harvest: pressing with a beam gives the second grade
steps.stepSummary: For the third harvest, the olives are pressed down with a beam. רבי יהודה says stones are used instead. This oil is the second grade.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then he presses the olives down with a beam. רבי יהודה says: with stones. This is the second grade.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה keeps describing the third harvest. After the first oil drips out, the olives are pressed to squeeze out more oil.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This works just like the second harvest in Step 15. The first oil dripped out by itself, and now real pressure is added. The תנא קמא uses a wooden beam, while רבי יהודה uses only stones. Either way, the result is the second grade of oil.

keyTerms.meaning: presses down, puts weight on top
a heavy wooden beam used to press olives
stones, a gentler kind of weight

phrases.english: He presses down with a beam,
Rabbi Yehuda says: with stones –
this is the second grade.

steps.triggerLanguage: טוֹעֵן בְּקוֹרָה, רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: בַּאֲבָנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the third harvest process from Step 18, moving from the first grade to the second.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Third harvest: pressing with a beam (רבי יהודה says stones) produces the second grade of oil.

steps.title: Third harvest: grinding and pressing again gives the third grade
steps.stepSummary: The olives are ground and pressed one more time. This oil is the third grade.
steps.simpleTranslation: He grinds again and presses again. This is the third grade.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה describes the last step of the third harvest, which squeezes out whatever oil is left.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the olives are ground with a millstone and pressed once more. This gets out the last oil, which is the lowest grade. It matches Step 16 for the second harvest.

keyTerms.meaning: ground the olives, as with a millstone
third, here meaning the third grade of oil

phrases.english: He went back, ground, and pressed –
this is the third grade.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the pressing process, producing the final grade.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Grinding and pressing again produces the third grade of oil.

steps.title: Third harvest: only the first grade goes to the מנורה
steps.stepSummary: For the third harvest's oils, only the first grade may be used for the מנורה. The other grades may be used for מנחות.
steps.simpleTranslation: The first grade is for the מנורה, and the rest are for מנחות.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes the third harvest by telling us which of its oils can be used for what.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same rule as Step 17 for the second harvest. The מנורה needs the purest oil, so only the first grade is used there. The second and third grades are still fine for מנחות.

keyTerms.meaning: the golden Candelabrum lit in the מקדש
meal offerings, which are mixed with oil
the rest, meaning the other grades

steps.whatToRemember: Every harvest makes three grades of oil. Only the first grade, the one that drips out on its own before any pressing, is used for the מנורה. All the other grades are used for מנחות.

phrases.english: The first – for the Candelabrum,
and the rest – for meal offerings.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the usage rule for the three grades just described, closing the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Third harvest: the first grade is for the מנורה, and the rest are for מנחות.

steps.title: What is the correct wording: מגרגרו or מגלגלו?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins by asking about the exact wording of the משנה. Does it say מגרגרו (he picks the ripe olives one by one) or מגלגלו (he waits until they all ripen)?
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was asked: did we learn 'מגרגרו' in the משנה, or did we learn 'מגלגלו'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts its discussion with a question about the wording of the משנה. This sets up the discussion that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two words look and sound almost the same, but they mean different things. מגרגרו means picking only the ripe olives at the top of the tree. מגלגלו means waiting until all the olives ripen and then picking them. The גמרא wants to know which one the משנה actually said.

keyTerms.meaning: a question was raised to them, meaning a real question the חכמים were unsure about
he picks the olives one by one, taking only the ripe ones
he lets the olives ripen first, then picks them all

steps.confusionAlert: This is not an argument about the הלכה itself. It is a question about which word is really written in the משנה. The two words differ by just one letter (ר versus ל), but the meaning changes.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
A question was raised before them:
Did we learn 'he picks them one by one,'
phrases.notes: This goes back to the first harvest earlier in the משנה, which spoke of picking the olives at the top of the tree.

phrases.english: or did we learn 'he lets them ripen'?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: מְגַרְגְּרוֹ תְּנַן, אוֹ מְגַלְגְּלוֹ תְּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The משנה has ended, and the גמרא opens with a question about its wording at the beginning (the first harvest).
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the משנה reads מגרגרו (picking the ripe olives one by one) or מגלגלו (letting them all ripen before picking).

steps.title: A ברייתא answers: the word is מגלגלו
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that learns from "שמן זית" that the oil should come from olives ripened on the tree. It uses the word מגלגלו for the first harvest and describes how the first grade of oil is made.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear a ברייתא: "Olive oil" means oil from olives that ripened on their tree. From here the Sages said: for the first olive harvest, one lets the olives ripen at the top of the tree. Then he brings them to the olive press, grinds them with a millstone, and puts them in baskets. The oil that drips out is the first grade.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question about the wording by quoting a ברייתא that clearly says מגלגלו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא reads the פסוק "שמן זית" as "oil from its olive tree", meaning the olives should be fully ripe before they are picked. That fits מגלגלו, letting the whole crop ripen, and not מגרגרו, picking olives one at a time. So the question from Step 22 is settled. The ברייתא then describes the first grade of oil, which drips out from the baskets by itself.

keyTerms.meaning: He lets the whole crop ripen on the tree (the reading the ברייתא supports)
From its olive tree, meaning olives that ripened on the tree
The olive-press building
Millstones used to grind the olives
Wicker baskets the ground olives are placed in

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the ברייתא is only about oil-making. It is quoted here because it uses the word מגלגלו, and that answers the wording question from Step 22.

phrases.english: Come and hear, as it is taught in a ברייתא:
"Olive oil" means from its olive tree,
phrases.notes: שמות 27:20. The idea is that the olives ripen fully while still on the tree.

phrases.english: From here they said:
For the first olive harvest, one lets it ripen at the top of the tree,
phrases.notes: Look at the word מגלגלו: that's the answer to the question from the last step.

phrases.english: and brings it into the olive-press building,
and grinds it with a millstone,
and places it in baskets.

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁמֶן הַיּוֹצֵא מִמֶּנּוּ, זֶה הָיָה רִאשׁוֹן.
phrases.english: The oil that comes out from it was the first grade.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the wording question raised in Step 22.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the משנה reads מגרגרו or מגלגלו.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ברייתא says מגלגלו, so the olives are left to ripen fully on the tree.

steps.title: Second and third grades, and how each grade is used
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: pressing with a beam gives the second grade, and grinding and pressing again gives the third. The first grade goes to the מנורה and the rest to מנחות. The second harvest works the same way.
steps.simpleTranslation: Next he presses the olives with a beam, and the oil that comes out is the second grade. Then he takes them out again, grinds them, and presses them, and that is the third grade. The first grade is for the מנורה and the rest is for מנחות. The second olive harvest is done the same way.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes describing the first harvest and says the second harvest follows the same process.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each extra amount of force gives a lower grade of oil. Only the purest oil, the first grade, is good enough for the מנורה, while the lower grades can still be used for מנחות. The words "וכן זית שני" tell us there is no need to describe the second harvest separately.

keyTerms.meaning: Pressed down with a heavy wooden beam
Unloaded, meaning he took the crushed olives out to grind them again
Meal offerings, which also need oil
The lamp in the מקדש, which needs the purest oil

phrases.english: He pressed it down with a beam;

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁמֶן הַיּוֹצֵא מִמֶּנּוּ – זֶה הָיָה שֵׁנִי,
phrases.english: the oil that comes out from it was the second grade,
and then he took them out again, ground them, and pressed them,
and this was the third grade.
The first is for the Menorah,
and the rest is for meal offerings.
And the same goes for the second olive harvest.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא, finishing the first harvest and including the second.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the first and second harvests, the first grade is for the מנורה and the second and third grades are for מנחות.

steps.title: The third harvest needs extra preparation
steps.stepSummary: For the third harvest, the olives are packed in the olive-press building until they soften, then dried on the roof in a heap until their fluids drain away. After that they are ground and placed in baskets, and the oil that drips out is the first grade.
steps.simpleTranslation: For the third olive harvest, he packs the olives in the olive-press building until they soften. Then he brings them up to the roof and piles them in a heap shaped like a palm tree until their fluids drain out. Then he brings them back to the olive press, grinds them with a millstone, and puts them in baskets. The oil that comes out is the first grade.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now describes the different process for the third harvest, which matches what the משנה said in Step 18.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The third harvest's olives are not fully ripe, so they must first soften in storage and then drip out their watery fluids on the roof. Only after that are they ground like the other harvests. The ברייתא adds a detail the משנה did not spell out: the olives are piled in a heap until the fluids drain away.

keyTerms.meaning: He packs or stores the olives together
Until it softens
Like a palm tree shape: a heap, wide at the bottom and narrow at the top
Until its watery fluids drip away

phrases.english: And for the third olive harvest,
he packs it in the olive-press building until it softens,
and brings it up to the roof,
and piles it up in the shape of a palm tree
until its fluids drain away,
and brings it into the olive-press building,
and grinds it with a millstone,
and places it in baskets,

phrases.aramaic: וָשֶׁמֶן הַיּוֹצֵא מִמֶּנּוּ – זֶה הָיָה רִאשׁוֹן.
phrases.english: and the oil that comes out from it was the first grade.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the first and second harvests to the special process for the third harvest.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Third-harvest olives are softened, drained on the roof, then ground; the oil that drips out is the first grade.

steps.title: Third harvest grades and their uses
steps.stepSummary: Pressing the third-harvest olives with a beam gives the second grade, and grinding and pressing again gives the third. Here too, the first grade is for the מנורה and the rest for מנחות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then he presses with a beam, and the oil that comes out is the second grade. He takes it out, grinds it again, and presses it, and that is the third grade. The first grade is for the מנורה and the rest is for מנחות.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא ends by giving the grades for the third harvest and the same rule about which oil goes where.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though the third harvest goes through extra steps, its first grade is still fit for the מנורה. This matches Step 21, where the משנה said the third harvest's first grade may be used for the מנורה. The same three-grade system applies to every harvest.

keyTerms.meaning: And the rest, meaning the second and third grades

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא proves the משנה says מגלגלו. In all three harvests, oil comes out in three grades: the first grade, which drips out without pressing, goes to the מנורה, and the pressed grades go to מנחות.

phrases.english: He pressed it down with a beam;

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁמֶן הַיּוֹצֵא מִמֶּנּוּ – זֶה הָיָה שֵׁנִי.
phrases.english: the oil that comes out from it was the second grade.
He took it out, ground it again, and pressed it,
and this was the third grade.
The first is for the Menorah,
and the rest is for meal offerings.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the third-harvest description and closes the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For the third harvest too, the first grade is for the מנורה and the second and third grades are for מנחות.

steps.title: רבי יהודה's gentler method of making the oil
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends with רבי יהודה, who says the olives are crushed in a mortar, not ground in a mill. They are pressed with stones, not a beam, and are set around the inner walls of the basket, not dropped into the basket.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: He would not grind the olives with millstones, but would crush them in a mortar. He would not press with a beam, but with stones. He would not put the olives into the baskets, but around the inside walls of the basket.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the last part of the ברייתא. רבי יהודה disagrees with the method described by the רבנן and gives his own way of making the oil.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה changes three things: crushing in a mortar instead of grinding with millstones, pressing with stones instead of a heavy beam, and lining the basket's walls instead of filling the basket. Each change is a gentler way of handling the olives.

keyTerms.meaning: Millstones, used to grind the olives
A mortar, where olives are crushed by pounding
A heavy wooden beam used to press the olives
Around the inside walls of the basket

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
He would not grind it with millstones,
rather, he would crush it in a mortar,
and he would not press with a beam
but rather with stones,
and he would not put it into the baskets
but rather around the inside of the basket.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא by adding רבי יהודה's dissenting method.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, the olives are crushed in a mortar, pressed with stones, and placed around the walls of the basket.

steps.title: Our משנה seems to follow two different opinions
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out a problem inside our משנה. It says to crush the olives, which is רבי יהודה's view. It also says to put them inside the basket, which is the view of the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: This משנה itself is difficult. Who says to crush? That is רבי יהודה. But 'into the basket' brings us to the רבנן!
steps.whatsHappening: Now that the ברייתא is clear, the גמרא goes back to our משנה. It shows that the משנה seems to mix two opinions that disagree with each other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא teaches that crushing belongs to רבי יהודה, while the רבנן grind. It also teaches that putting olives inside the basket belongs to the רבנן, while רבי יהודה lines the walls. Our משנה says both 'crush' and 'inside the basket', so it seems to follow neither opinion fully.

keyTerms.meaning: This text itself is difficult; it contradicts itself
Whose view is this?
We have come to the view of the רבנן
He crushes (by pounding)

phrases.english: This itself is difficult:
phrases.notes: 'This' is our משנה, which says the olives are crushed and then put into the basket.

phrases.english: Crushing — whose view is it?
It is Rabbi Yehuda's,
yet 'into the basket' — we have come to the Rabbis!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the dispute in the ברייתא to raise a problem about our משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The wording of our משנה: 'crush it and put it into the basket'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The two parts of the משנה match two opposing sides of the ברייתא, so the משנה appears to contradict itself.

steps.title: The משנה's author agrees on one point and disagrees on the other
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the תנא of our משנה agrees with רבי יהודה about crushing. He disagrees with him about where the olives are placed in the basket.
steps.simpleTranslation: This תנא agrees with רבי יהודה on one point and disagrees with him on another.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the problem. The משנה is not mixed up. Its author simply holds a view of his own that matches רבי יהודה only partly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is no rule that a תנא must accept all of someone's opinions or none of them. The author of our משנה agrees with רבי יהודה that the olives are crushed. He does not agree about lining the basket, so he places them inside it.

keyTerms.meaning: The teacher of the משנה or ברייתא
He holds like him
He disagrees with him

steps.whatToRemember: Our משנה follows רבי יהודה on crushing the olives, but follows its own view, like the רבנן, on putting them inside the basket.

phrases.aramaic: הַאי תַּנָּא סָבַר לַהּ כְּוָתֵיהּ בַּחֲדָא,
phrases.english: This tanna agrees with him on one point,
phrases.notes: 'Him' is רבי יהודה, and the one point is crushing the olives.

phrases.english: and disagrees with him on another.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַאי תַּנָּא סָבַר לַהּ כְּוָתֵיהּ בַּחֲדָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 28.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Split opinion: the author of the משנה agrees with one sage on one detail and not on another
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה must follow one side completely, so it seems to contradict itself.
steps.terutzMaskana: The author of the משנה agrees with רבי יהודה about crushing but disagrees about placement in the basket.

steps.title: New משנה: ranking the nine grades of oil
steps.stepSummary: The משנה ranks the nine kinds of oil (three grades from each of three harvests) from best to worst, grouping the ones of equal quality.
steps.simpleTranslation: The first grade of the first harvest is the best of all. The second grade of the first harvest and the first grade of the second harvest are equal. The third grade of the first harvest, the second of the second, and the first of the third are equal. The third of the second and the second of the third are equal. The third grade of the third harvest is the lowest of all.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It takes the nine oils described earlier and lines them up in five levels of quality.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The pattern works like stairs: moving down one grade has the same effect on quality as moving to a later harvest. So oils whose grade number plus harvest number add up to the same total are equal. The best is first-of-first and the worst is third-of-third.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
The first grade of oil from the first harvest
There is nothing better than it
Equal in quality
There is nothing lower than it

steps.confusionAlert: In each pair, the first number is the grade of oil and the second is the harvest. So 'הַשֵּׁנִי שֶׁבָּרִאשׁוֹן' means the second grade of oil from the first harvest, not the reverse.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
The first of the first — there is none above it.
phrases.notes: Read it as: the first grade of oil from the first harvest.

phrases.english: The second of the first and the first of the second are equal.
The third of the first and the second of the second
and the first of the third are equal.
The third of the second and the second of the third are equal.
The third of the third — there is none below it.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ הָרִאשׁוֹן שֶׁבָּרִאשׁוֹן אֵין לְמַעְלָה הֵימֶנּוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה that ranks the nine oils described in the previous משנה (steps 9–21).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The nine oils fall into five levels of quality. First-of-first is the best, third-of-third is the worst, and the oils in between are grouped as equals.

steps.title: A logical argument that meal offerings should need the best oil
steps.stepSummary: The משנה suggests a קל וחומר: if the מנורה, which is not eaten, needs refined olive oil, then מנחות, which are eaten, should need it all the more.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think all meal offerings should need refined olive oil. After all, the מנורה is not eaten and still needs refined olive oil. Meal offerings are eaten, so shouldn't they need refined olive oil even more?
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה lays out a reasonable-sounding argument that מנחות should also need the best oil. This sets up the next step, where the argument will be rejected.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a קל וחומר, a 'lesser to greater' argument. Something eaten seems more important than something only burned for light. So if the 'lesser' case, the מנורה, needs top oil, the 'greater' case, the מנחות, should need it too.

keyTerms.meaning: A 'lesser to greater' logical argument
It would make sense by logic
Pure, refined olive oil (the top grade)
Requires
For eating

phrases.english: Also, all the meal offerings

phrases.aramaic: הָיוּ בַּדִּין שֶׁיִּטְעֲנוּ שֶׁמֶן זַיִת זָךְ,
phrases.english: it would be logical that they should require refined olive oil,
since if the מנורה, which is not for eating,
requires refined olive oil,
then meal offerings, which are for eating,

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ דִּין שֶׁיִּטְעֲנוּ שֶׁמֶן זַיִת זָךְ!
phrases.english: is it not logical that they should require refined olive oil!
phrases.notes: This is said as a strong question, but it is only a 'you might think.' The next line will knock it down.

steps.triggerLanguage: אף כל המנחות היו בדין שיטענו שמן זית זך
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After ranking the oils, the משנה asks whether מנחות should also need the top grade that the מנורה uses.
steps.raayaObject: That מנחות should require שמן זית זך
steps.raayaSupportSource: A קל וחומר from the מנורה: its oil is not eaten yet still needs refined oil.

steps.title: The verse limits refined oil to lighting
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק 'זך כתית למאור' shows that refined, pounded oil is required for lighting the מנורה, not for מנחות.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says 'refined, pounded, for lighting.' This means refined, pounded oil is needed for lighting, but not for meal offerings.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה rejects the קל וחומר from the last step by pointing to the exact words of the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'למאור' (for lighting) ties the requirement of 'זך כתית' to the מנורה alone. A clear פסוק beats a logical argument. So the special requirement stays with the מנורה and is not carried over to מנחות.

keyTerms.meaning: The verse teaches (used to bring a פסוק that settles the question)
Pounded or crushed (the olives are crushed, not ground)
For lighting

steps.whatToRemember: A קל וחומר would have required top oil for מנחות, but the פסוק 'זך כתית למאור' limits that requirement to the מנורה.
steps.confusionAlert: The משנה does not say the מנורה is more important than מנחות. It only says the פסוק ties this oil requirement to lighting, so the logic of 'eaten is more important' does not decide the question.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains the earlier rule that the first-grade oil goes to the מנורה and the other grades go to מנחות.

phrases.english: The verse teaches:
"Refined, pounded, for lighting"
but refined, pounded oil is not needed for meal offerings.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It rejects the קל וחומר of step 31 by using the wording of the פסוק.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the whole קל וחומר that would have required refined oil for מנחות.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The פסוק itself says the refined, pounded oil is 'for lighting', so logic cannot extend the rule to מנחות.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Refined, pounded olive oil is required for the מנורה, not for מנחות.
